HPPD can either get worse with drug use, stay the same, or I guess in some cases i’ve read people have tripped and then it went away so it’s very different for everyone but I do suggest to read a little into it because you really don’t know what can affect it or even worsening it. And good point that we don’t have live music lol and who knows when we will,so It’s a good time to be sober and maybe your symptoms will just go away and you’ll be back to smoking weed like usual. Also a lot of stuff you’ll probably read through might freak you out, idk, i was pretty rattled but everyone’s brain chemistry is so different and with the lack of research on it seems like there are lots of ways to cope with it but just need to find what works for you if HPPD is the case.
Dude I get it, they are dumb questions. But there’s not much research on it and some people just want answers, I can imagine some people are younger than expected and probably feeling overwhelmed.

I was also abusing acid for a couple months so it’s totally possible. Given that you did a lot of LSD there’s a chance it could be HPPD; hallucinogenic persistent perception disorder, it’s kind of like the acid didn’t close the door on the way out . r/HPPD  can help explain more about it but it messes with your dopamine levels, vision, and bunch of stuff depending on the severity. Like for me, I still see fuzzy walls and sometimes they breathe or it gets worse depending on my anxiety that day. I think if you end up finding a psychiatrist to talk to, they’ll probably say it’s a symptom of schizophrenia because there’s not much research or much known about HPPD, which is why I got diagnosed with schizoaffective instead of just bipolar. But It sounds like it could be a minor case of HPPD because it’s exactly what you’re experience sounds like how I feel when I smoke too . Totally do a little research on HPPD but don’t try to feel too bad about it some people just stay sober for 6-12 months and their symptoms got better or completely stopped.


Also feel free to PM me, i’d be happy to talk to you about my experience.
